facts.statement: Gryposuchus is an extinct genus of gavialid crocodilian, meaning "hooked crocodile".
facts.quote: Gryposuchus (meaning "hooked crocodile") is an extinct genus of gavialid crocodilian.

facts.statement: The type species Gryposuchus jessei was named in 1912 based on a well-preserved rostrum found along the Pauini River in Brazil.
facts.quote: The type species of Gryposuchus is G. jessei, named based on a well-preserved rostrum collected along the Pauini River of Brazil in 1912.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Gryposuchus jessei was likely destroyed in 1943 during the bombing of Hamburg in World War II.
facts.quote: The specimen was probably destroyed during World War II by the 1943 bombing of Hamburg.

facts.statement: Gryposuchus pachakamue was named in 2016 by Rodolfo Salas-Gismondi and colleagues based on skull material from the Pebas Formation in the Peruvian Amazon.
facts.quote: Some skull material also recovered from Peruvian Amazon (Iquitos) in the Pebas Formation of the Middle Miocene, was named as Gryposuchus pachakamue in 2016 by Rodolfo Salas-Gismondi et al.

facts.statement: Gryposuchus pachakamue is characterized by non-telescoped orbits, suggesting that this trait may have evolved independently in gryposuchines and gavialines in riverine environments.
facts.quote: This new species is characterized by orbits that did not protude upwards ("telescoped") as some gryposuchines and gavialines (like the modern gharial), which implies that both groups might have evolved this characteristic independently in fluvial enviroments.

facts.statement: Gryposuchus lived during the Miocene epoch, specifically from the Colhuehuapian to the Huayquerian ages.
facts.quote: The genus existed during the Miocene epoch (Colhuehuapian to Huayquerian).

facts.statement: Fossils of Gryposuchus have been found in Argentina, Colombia, Venezuela, Brazil, and the Peruvian Amazon.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from Argentina, Colombia, Venezuela, Brazil and the Peruvian Amazon.

facts.statement: Gryposuchus was likely the most successful gryposuchine in South America because it was adapted to freshwater environments, unlike many related species that lived in estuarine, coastal, or marine waters.
facts.quote: This dominance was likely due to the fact that Gryposuchus was one of only two freshwater adapted gryposuchines (other than Hesperogavialis), whereas the others (such as Siquisiquesuchus and Piscogavialis) were either primarily estuarine, coastal or marine based predators.

facts.statement: The aridification of the continental interior and the filling of wetland basins likely caused the extinction of Gryposuchus by restricting space and food resources for these large, specialized crocodilians.
facts.quote: The co-current aridification of the continental interior, and filling of peripheral wetland basins, further restricted the space and food resources of these large, food-intensive specialist crocodilians, and was probably the primary cause of their extinction.

facts.statement: Gryposuchus is the type genus of the subfamily Gryposuchinae, though a 2018 study suggests this group might be paraphyletic and represents an evolutionary grade leading to the gharial.
facts.quote: Gryposuchus is the type genus of the subfamily Gryposuchinae, although a 2018 study indicates that Gryposuchinae and Gryposuchus might be paraphyletic and rather an evolutionary grade towards the gharial.

facts.statement: It is debated whether G. neogaeus and G. colombianus are synonyms of G. jessei, but most researchers consider them distinct species due to significant anatomical differences.
facts.quote: G. neogaeus and G. colombianus have been proposed as synonyms of G. jessei, but this is unlikely due to the number of anatomical differences between them.

facts.statement: A 2007 phylogenetic analysis placed Gryposuchus within the subfamily Gryposuchinae alongside the genera Aktiogavialis, Ikanogavialis, Piscogavialis, and Siquisiquesuchus.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis conducted in a 2007 study found Gryposuchinae to include the genera Aktiogavialis, Gryposuchus, Ikanogavialis, Piscogavialis, and Siquisiquesuchus.

facts.statement: At the Miocene/Pliocene boundary, all Gavialoidea and Crocodyloidea were likely extirpated from South America.
facts.quote: At the Miocene/Pliocene boundary, all Gavialoidea and Crocodyloidea (another superfamily colonising in the Miocene) were likely extirpated from South America

facts.statement: The type species Gryposuchus jessei was named in 1912 based on a well-preserved snout collected along the Pauini River in Brazil.
facts.quote: La especie tipo de Gryposuchus es G. jessei, nombrada con base en un hocico bien preservado recolectado a lo largo del río Pauini en Brasil en 1912.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of G. jessei was likely destroyed in 1943 during the bombing of Hamburg in World War II.
facts.quote: El espécimen probablemente fue destruido durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial durante el bombardeo de Hamburgo en 1943.

facts.statement: A specimen named UFAC 1272, consisting of a premaxilla and a maxilla, was discovered in 1997 at the Sena Madureia site in the Late Miocene Solimões Formation.
facts.quote: Otro espécimen denominado UFAC 1272, consistente de un premaxilar y un maxilar, fue descubierto en el yacimiento cercano de Sena Madureia de la Formación Solimões de finales del Mioceno, y fue referido a esta especies en 1997.

facts.statement: The species G. neogaeus was included in the genus in 1982, though its specimens were originally described in 1885 from the Late Miocene Ituzaingó Formation in Argentina and referred to Rhamphostomopsis at the time.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie, G. neogaeus, fue incluida en el género en 1982; los especímenes de la misma fueron descritos originalmente de la Formación Ituzaingó de finales del Mioceno de Argentina en 1885, aunque por entonces fue referido a Rhamphostomopsis.

facts.statement: The species G. colombianus was named in 1965 from Middle Miocene deposits in Colombia and Late Miocene formations in Venezuela, and was originally referred to the modern genus Gavialis.
facts.quote: Otra especie, G. colombianus, fue recuperada de depósitos de Colombia que datan del Mioceno medio del Grupo Honda en Colombia y finales del Mioceno de la Formación Urumaco en Venezuela. Esta especie, nombrada en 1965, fue originalmente referida al moderno género Gavialis.

facts.statement: Cranial materials from the Pebas Formation in Iquitos, Peru, were named Gryposuchus pachakamue in 2016 by Rodolfo Salas-Gismondi and colleagues.
facts.quote: También se ha recuperado algunos materiales craneanos en la Amazonía peruana (Iquitos) en la Formación Pebas, y fueron nombrados como Gryposuchus pachakamue en 2016 por Rodolfo Salas-Gismondi et al.

facts.statement: G. pachakamue is characterized by having 22 teeth in both the jaw and maxilla, a snout length comparable to the modern Gavialis gangeticus, and eye orbits that were wider than long and less rotated upward than in other gavialids, implying it lacked fully developed telescopic eyes.
facts.quote: Esta nueva especie se caracteriza por tener 22 dientes tanto en la mandíbula como en el maxilar, un hocico cn una longitud relativa comparable a la del actual Gavialis gangeticus, y es notable porque sus órbitas oculares eran más anchas que largas y no tan vueltas hacia arriba como en otras especies de gaviálidos, incluyendo a los griposuquinos, lo cual implica que G. pachakamue no tenía totalmente desarrollada la condición de órbitas "telescópicas" (ojos sobresalientes).

facts.statement: The species G. croizati, described in 2009, was found in the Urumaco Formation in northeastern Venezuela and is distinguished by a reduced number of maxillary teeth, a thin interfenestral parietal bar, and a widely separated and reduced palatal fenestra.
facts.quote: Una especie descrita en 2009, G. croizati, fue hallada en la formación geológica Urumaco en el nororiente de Venezuela, la cual puede ser distinguida de las otras especies de Gryposuchus sobre la base de su reducido número de dientes maxilares, una delgada barra interfenestral parietal, y una ampliamente separada y reducida fenestra palatal, entre otras cosas.

facts.statement: Based on orbital skeleton measurements, G. croizati is estimated to have reached a total length of 10.15 meters and a mass of approximately 1,745 kilograms.
facts.quote: Basándose en las medidas del esqueleto orbital, se ha estimado que la longitud total del animal llegaba a los 10.15 metros, con una masa total de cerca de 1.745 kilogramos.

facts.statement: G. pachakamue inhabited the proto-Amazonian river system 13 million years ago and represents the oldest record of gavialids in that area, suggesting its primitive telescopic eye condition evolved convergently with Asian Gavialis species.
facts.quote: Dado que esta especie, que habitó el sistema fluvial protoamazónico hace 13 millones de años, es el registro más antiguo de gaviálidos en esa área y tenía una condición primitiva de ojos telescópicos, sugiere que el desarrollo de dicha condición fue un caso de evolución convergente con las especies de Gavialis también halladas en ambientes fluviales en Asia.

facts.statement: A 2007 phylogenetic analysis determined that the subfamily Gryposuchinae includes the genera Aktiogavialis, Gryposuchus, Ikanogavialis, Piscogavialis, and Siquisiquesuchus.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético llevada a cabo en 2007 determinó que la subfamilia Gryposuchinae incluye a los géneros Aktiogavialis, Gryposuchus, Ikanogavialis, Piscogavialis y Siquisiquesuchus.

facts.statement: The genus Gryposuchus was named by Gürich in 1912.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Gryposuchus (genus), Gürich 1912

facts.statement: Gryposuchus belongs to the subfamily Gryposuchinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Gryposuchinae

facts.statement: Gryposuchus is classified within the family Gavialidae.
facts.quote: Family: Gavialidae

facts.statement: Gryposuchus is a member of the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The time range for Gryposuchus spans from the Burdigalian to the Late Pleistocene, approximately 20.45 to 0.0117 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Burdigalian to Late Pleistocene (20.45 to 0.0117 million years ago)

facts.statement: G. jessei has also been reported from the Urumaco Formation in northwestern Venezuela.
facts.quote: G. jessei también ha sido reportado en la Formación Urumaco en el noroeste de Venezuela.

facts.statement: G. colombianus was originally referred to the modern genus Gavialis when it was named in 1965.
facts.quote: Esta especie, nombrada en 1965, fue originalmente referida al moderno género Gavialis.

facts.statement: Fragmentary Gryposuchus materials from the Fitzcarrald area in Peruvian Amazonia date to the Late Miocene and are similar to G. colombianus but differ in facial proportions.
facts.quote: Materiales fragmentarios de Gryposuchus de la zona de Fitzcarrald en la Amazonia peruana datan de finales del Mioceno y son bastante parecidos a G. colombianus, si bien difieren en las proporciones del rostro.

facts.statement: The species name G. pachakamue references the Quechua term for a primordial god and "narrator".
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie es una referencia al término quechua para un dios primordial y "narrador".

facts.statement: Although Gryposuchus reached Argentina by the Middle Miocene, known species diversity peaked in the Late Miocene with four to five species present, three of which coexisted in the Urumaco Formation.
facts.quote: Aunque Gryposuchus había alcanzado Argentina a mediados del Mioceno, la diversidad conocida de especies alcanzó su cima a finales del Mioceno, con cuatro a cinco especies presentes, tres de las cuales coexistieron en la Formación Urumaco.

facts.statement: The extinction of Gavialoidea and Crocodyloidea in South America was likely caused by the continued uplift of the northern Andes, which redirected Caribbean river mouths to the colder Atlantic and transformed hyperdiverse crocodilian wetlands into a fully developed river delta system.
facts.quote: Esto probablemente se debió a la continua elevación de las secciones del norte de la cordillera de los Andes creando la futura cuenca amazónica, al redireccionar el flujo de las desembocaduras del Caribe al más frío Atlántico, y transformando los megahumedales responsables de la híperdiversidad de crocodilianos en un sistema fluvial de desembocaduras totalmente desarrollado.
